verdict.rationale: Appwrite Functions provide first-party background automation: functions can be triggered by server events, webhooks and scheduled executions, and the product page advertises cron jobs and event handlers running in isolated runtimes. That covers recurring, unattended execution, not just one-off actions. The AI-native angle is thin, though: nothing shows agent-driven or AI-orchestrated automations that run on their own. Missing for 10: documented AI/agent-driven autonomous automation workflows, depth on schedule configuration and monitoring of background runs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: These Functions can be triggered by HTTP requests, SDK methods, server events, webhooks, and scheduled executions.
Run API endpoints, webhooks, cron jobs, and event handlers in secure isolated runtimes that scale with demand.
Respond to server events in realtime.
